exactPassages: Sidewalk cafes provided beyond the building line shall comply with the requirements of this section, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and with the projection limitations of Chapter 32 of this code.
No part of any awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment or removable platform of a sidewalk cafe shall be located:
2. So as to obstruct any exit from a building;
3. So as to obstruct any cellar access hatch or areaway;

Exception: Upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform, designed in accordance with Section 3111.5, to cover a cellar entrance or areaway that is not used as a required means of egress.
Sidewalk cafes and access thereto shall comply with Chapter 11.

Where dining surfaces for the consumption of food or drink are provided, at least 10 percent of the total number of seating and standing spaces, but not less than one, of each type of dining surfaces shall be accessible and be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

Unless separated from seating inside the building by fire partitions complying with Section 713 , the seating for enclosed sidewalk cafes shall be added to that inside the building in order to determine whether a place of assembly certificate of operation is required.

testCase.question: A restaurant proposes a sidewalk café with furniture near a building exit and cellar hatch. The owner says outdoor-dining authorization allows the exterior seats to be counted separately from the interior PACO and eliminates further accessibility review. The documents do not say whether the café is beyond the building line, enclosed, or separated from the interior seating by a Section 713 fire partition. What can be concluded from the selected Building Code passages, and what remains unresolved?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The proposal cannot be approved from the selected evidence. If it is a sidewalk café beyond the building line, BC 3111.1 requires compliance not only with Section 3111 but also with Chapter 32 and separate zoning and agency requirements; the selected evidence does not provide those outside rules. BC 3111.4 prohibits café components from obstructing a building exit or cellar hatch. Its cellar-entrance exception is not automatic: it requires a special application, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and a cellar entrance or areaway that is not required egress. BC 3111.6 makes Chapter 11 applicable to the café and its access. BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with not less than one accessible space at each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed and located on a level served by an accessible route. BC 3111.7 supplies only a conditional rule for an enclosed sidewalk café: unless a Section 713 fire partition separates it from inside seating, its seating is added to the inside seating solely to determine whether a PACO is required. These passages do not establish the approved interior capacity, the treatment of every open exterior seating arrangement, property-line or operational jurisdiction, DOT authorization, electrical permitting, or overall approval.

expectedUncertainty.description: The selected passages establish several conditional Building Code constraints, but they do not establish overall approval, current agency jurisdiction, lawful seating capacity, or electrical and operational requirements.

answer.answerText:
The owner’s claimed authorization does not, on the selected Building Code evidence, allow exterior seats to be counted separately in all cases or eliminate accessibility review. If the café is beyond the building line, it must comply with BC 3111, the Zoning Resolution, the requirements of the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and Chapter 32 projection limitations. The supplied provision does not establish that a particular authorization has been obtained or that it overrides those requirements.

Sidewalk-café awnings, enclosures, fixtures, equipment, and removable platforms may not obstruct a building exit, cellar access hatch, or areaway. A cellar entrance or areaway may be covered only by an easily removable, prominently designated platform designed under BC 3111.5, and then only upon special application and commissioner permission; the entrance or areaway cannot be used as a required means of egress. Furniture near the exit and hatch therefore cannot be found compliant from the stated facts alone.

Accessibility review remains required: the sidewalk café and its access must comply with Chapter 11. Separately, where dining surfaces are provided, BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating or standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total number of such spaces, and at least one accessible dining surface of each type. Those accessible dining surfaces must be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route. The counts, dining-surface types and locations, distribution, and route information are not supplied, so a final accessibility count or compliance finding cannot be made.

The selected code addresses separate counting only for an enclosed sidewalk café and only when determining whether a place of assembly certificate of operation is required. Its seats must be added to interior seats unless the café is separated from interior seating by fire partitions complying with BC 713. Since enclosure status and the claimed BC 713 separation are unknown, the selected evidence does not resolve whether the counts must be combined for that certificate determination. It establishes no general permission to count exterior seating separately for PACO or another purpose.
answer.conclusion: The owner’s claimed authorization does not, on the selected Building Code evidence, allow exterior seats to be counted separately in all cases or eliminate accessibility review. If the café is beyond the building line, it must comply with BC 3111, the Zoning Resolution, the requirements of the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and Chapter 32 projection limitations. The supplied provision does not establish that a particular authorization has been obtained or that it overrides those requirements.

supportedPoints.heading: Beyond-building-line cafés have additional compliance obligations
supportedPoints.explanation: A sidewalk café provided beyond the building line must comply with BC 3111, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the requirements of the Commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and Chapter 32 projection limitations.

supportedPoints.heading: Café elements cannot obstruct exits or cellar access
supportedPoints.explanation: No awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment, or removable platform of a sidewalk café may obstruct a building exit, cellar access hatch, or areaway. The limited exception allows a commissioner, upon special application, to permit an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under BC 3111.5 over a cellar entrance or areaway that is not used as a required means of egress.

supportedPoints.heading: Café and its access remain subject to Chapter 11
supportedPoints.explanation: Sidewalk cafés and access to them must comply with Chapter 11.

supportedPoints.heading: Dining surfaces have quantified accessibility requirements
supportedPoints.explanation: Where dining surfaces for consuming food or drink are provided, accessible seating and standing spaces must equal at least 10 percent of the total number of those spaces. In addition, at least one dining surface of each type must be accessible. Accessible dining surfaces must be distributed throughout the facility and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

supportedPoints.heading: Enclosed café seating may need to be added to interior seating
supportedPoints.explanation: For determining whether a place of assembly certificate of operation is required, seating for an enclosed sidewalk café must be added to interior seating unless the café is separated from the interior seating by fire partitions complying with BC 713.
